chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja‘far, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about knowledge: “Is it a knowledge that the knowledgeable one learns from the mouths of men, or is it in the Book with you, which you read and thereby come to know from it?” He said: “The matter is greater than that and more binding. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:”
“And thus We revealed to you a Spirit from Our command; you did not know what the Book was, nor the faith.”

Then he said: “What do your companions say regarding this verse? Do they affirm that he was in a state in which he did not know what the Book was, nor the faith?” So I said: “I do not know, may I be your ransom, what they say.”

He said to me: “Yes, he indeed was in a state in which he did not know what the Book was, nor the faith, until Allah, the Exalted, sent the Spirit that is mentioned in the Book. Then when He revealed it to him, He taught by it the knowledge and the understanding. And it is the Spirit that Allah, the Exalted, gives to whomever He wills; so when He gives it to a servant, He teaches him understanding.”

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our command, referring to Allah’s command

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the verse about the Spirit from Allah’s command and the Prophet’s knowledge of the Book and faith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the knowledge in question is not merely acquired from people or by ordinary reading, but is connected to a divinely bestowed Spirit from the command of Allah. It comments on the verse by describing how knowledge and understanding were taught through this Spirit, and presents it as a gift Allah grants to whom He wills.
